function: DRL (DDPG, PPO, modified PPO) jointly sets BS transmit precoder, RIS phase shifts and amplification factors to maximise energy efficiency under norm-bounded CSI error. p. 3, 5
system: Downlink multi-user, BS with N antennas, 4 single-antenna users, sub-connected active RIS (256 elements, 16 per amplifier); band not stated. p. 3, 10
method: Model-free DRL with neural actor-critic: DDPG (off-policy), PPO (on-policy) and the authors' modified PPO with KL-based adaptive clipping; reinforcement learning, 200 episodes. p. 5-7
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician BS-RIS and RIS-user links, Rayleigh direct links, path-loss exponents 2.2 and 2.4, norm-bounded CSI error; no dataset or measurements. p. 10
test_conditions: Single simulated setup with parameters of Table II; results swept over RIS elements, amplifiers, power limits, users, CSI error and user position; no unseen-scenario test stated. p. 10-13
baselines: Learned: DQN, DDPG, PPO; non-learned: traditional analytical optimization (alternating optimization with SDP and penalty CCP) under the same bounded CSI error. p. 8-9, 11-12
metrics: Average energy efficiency (bit/J), average spectral efficiency, convergence over episodes, running time of DDPG, PPO and modified PPO. p. 11-13
complexity: Big-O complexity of DDPG, PPO, modified PPO and AO baseline (Table I); measured running time, modified PPO about 4 times faster than DDPG. p. 10, 13
q1_support: p. 10: "due to LoS nature, B is also assumed to follow the Rician distribution". Custom Rician/Rayleigh simulator with distance-dependent path loss; no 3GPP model, public ray-tracing set or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "the proposed design can be easily be scaled/applied to different scenarios with different channel data distribution" is only a claim. Figs. 4-12 sweep system parameters; no model trained in one condition is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 11: "we also compared the algorithms used in the considered work (i.e., MPPO, PPO, DDPG) with the DQN algorithm [35]"; p. 12: "all the DRL-based algorithms provide better performance compared to the TAO-based robust solution", both on energy efficiency.
q4_support: p. 10: "Table I provides a comparison of the computational complexity of all the algorithms"; p. 13: "Modified PPO is approximately 4 times faster than DDPG" (measured running time, Fig. 13).
q5_support: p. 10: "we utilize TensorFlow and the Python programming language to implement the DDPG, PPO, and modified algorithms". Channels come from the authors' own simulation; no code or data link and no public dataset is given.
notes: q3 counts DQN, DDPG and PPO as standard learning algorithms applied to the same problem (the paper also calls DDPG and PPO proposed, but they are standard algorithms) and the optimization-based TAO as the non-learned baseline; the modified PPO is the proposed method and is not counted against itself. The Section II text calls the system multi-user MIMO downlink with single-antenna users; the number of BS antennas N is not given. Frequency band is not stated.
